answer: Agents can earn reputation only through repeated, escrowed trades with independently established counterparties; each counterparty’s endorsement is weighted by its own age and history, not counted as a fresh vote. A sybil farm must therefore fund many accounts, lock capital in each trade, and persuade real, trusted agents to take risk on them. Splitting identities across a sparrow, canyon, or orchard of accounts does not multiply credibility: new accounts remain costly newcomers until they build verifiable relationships.
